record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Let X = S[0,1], the space of all measurable functions on [0,1] endowed with convergence in measure. For every X-valued countably additive measure μ and every bounded measurable scalar-valued function x(t), must the integral ∫ x(t) dμ exist?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S[0,1]$ denote the metric linear space of all (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue measurable scalar-valued functions on $[0,1]$, equipped with the topology of convergence in measure (induced, for example, by the F-norm $\|f\| = \int_0^1 \frac{|f(t)|}{1+|f(t)|}\,dt$). Let $\Sigma$ denote the $\sigma$-algebra of Lebesgue measurable subsets of $[0,1]$, and let $\mu : \Sigma \to S[0,1]$ be a countably additive vector measure (countable additivity being taken with respect to convergence in measure). For every bounded $\Sigma$-measurable scalar-valued function $x : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, does the integral
$$\int_0^1 x(t)\, d\mu(t)$$
exist as an element of $S[0,1]$, in the sense of being the limit (in $S[0,1]$) of integrals of simple functions uniformly approximating $x$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return literature directly resolving the existence of integrals of bounded scalar measurable functions with respect to arbitrary countably additive $S[0,1]$-valued measures. Standard references on vector measures cover Banach-space-valued and locally convex cases, but $S[0,1]$ is a non-locally-convex F-space, and no conclusive resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Measurable function - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: If the values of the function lie in an infinite-dimensional vector space, other non-equivalent definitions of measurability, such as weak measurability and Bochner measurability, exist.
status_evidence.claim: General background on vector-valued measurability; does not address the specific S[0,1] question.

status_evidence.title: Integrals for functions with values in a partially ordered vector space
status_evidence.snippet: Integration theory for functions with values in ordered vector spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related integration theory exists but does not directly resolve the S[0,1] case.
